subject.title: Widget token/cost data should follow the global refresh frequency instead of a fixed hourly TTL

question: Should automatic token/cost scans follow the global refresh frequency, or remain independently throttled because local history scans can be expensive?
rationale: Recent merged work deliberately preserved slower asynchronous scanning, so switching to the potentially one-minute global cadence requires an explicit performance and UX policy choice.

options.title: Global cadence with safeguards
options.body: Use the configured global interval for eligibility while preserving coalescing and adding a minimum interval or timeout backoff for expensive scans.

options.title: Separate token cadence
options.body: Keep token scans independent but add a dedicated setting and matching widget/preferences copy so the slower cadence is explicit.

options.title: Retain hourly policy
options.body: Keep hourly automatic scans and clearly document that global refresh frequency applies to provider quota refreshes rather than local token history.

recommendation.title: Global cadence with safeguards
recommendation.body: Use the configured global interval for eligibility while preserving coalescing and adding a minimum interval or timeout backoff for expensive scans.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history ties this person most directly to refresh-loop and widget token policy decisions.
